My friend was a loner. The perfect scenario for him to become a mass murderer. He was disillusioned about the system and his life in general. I approached his parents and siblings, they were willing to have me edge him closer to treatment. He of course was not only worried about seeking help but also the label and associated stigma that often comes when a person is diagnosed with an ailment. I researched support groups for his condition in our area and met them before talking to my friend. I was given some material to read and given the name of reliable doctors that were not only familiar with the condition but had family members suffering from the same condition. Said doctors were very helpful in setting a plan for treatment that was tailored to his needs. I went to the first few meetings and did most of the talking, this eventually got my very reclusive friend to share his thoughts and feelings. Prior to this meeting, he would talk only to me. Before I was even aware of his condition I tried to get him to meet new people, become more social. At first he would not talk to these people, but after seeing his best friend create a more tight knit circle that fit his personality, he became more open and was able to talk about openly with other people about his condition. Having vetted these people, I was able to make sure he was in good hands. With the proper support he pulled through and became a social monster LOL in school he started participating in activities that helped him channel his creative and zany side. I never lost what I loved about my friend, only the more sinister nature of his thoughts, especially the ones relating to cutting and dangerous behavior. His parents <adopted> me as part of the family because they could see my intentions were genuine. This is the most important part.
